content:
Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Razor clams

The Atlantic jackknife or razor clam is described through the knowledge needed to recognize its presence in tidal ground. The entry remembers the contrast between hand gathering and later mechanized extraction.1

Places named in the catalogue

Shinnecock Bay; Great South Bay.1

Hard clams / quahogs

Hard clams connect Shinnecock meals with tools, agriculture, and wampum. The catalogue describes white and purple shell beads as meaningful objects within relationships of exchange, and distinguishes those relationships from the monetary value imposed in colonial trade.2

Places named in the catalogue

Great South Bay; Shinnecock Bay; Peconic Bay; Montauk Bay.2

Soft-shell clams / steamers

Steamers are remembered as food gathered with clam rakes from tidal areas. The catalogue also records concern in 2013 about changing estuarine conditions and the survival of formerly abundant clams.3

Places named in the catalogue

Long Island Sound; Atlantic Ocean; Shinnecock Bay; Mecox Bay; Montauk Bay; Peconic Bay; Napeague Bay; Great South Bay.3

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF pp. 6–7. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
